findings.description: The axis model says each PolicyGuard input has exactly one primary axis, but later this fixture uses `risk_state` in both CapitalRiskAxis and SystemIntegrityAxis. That leaves the dual-impact path ambiguous for a trading-permission input and can produce divergent implementations.

evidence.quote: - **Primary assignment rule:** Every PolicyGuard input signal MUST have exactly one primary axis.

findings.proposed_fix: Explicitly allowlist `risk_state` as dual-impact or split it into axis-specific predicates so each input has one primary axis.

findings.description: The fixture makes missing/unparseable/stale critical inputs fail closed, but the listed ATs do not prove that behavior across the broader critical-input set. That leaves fail-closed TradingMode behavior under-specified for untested critical inputs.

evidence.quote: - Any critical PolicyGuard input missing/unparseable/stale per §2.2.1.2

findings.proposed_fix: Add ATs for representative non-session critical inputs proving ReduceOnly plus `REDUCEONLY_INPUT_MISSING_OR_STALE`.

findings.description: Reason completeness is normative for the winning tier, but the acceptance tests only prove multi-reason completeness for ReduceOnly. No listed AT forces simultaneous Kill predicates and checks that all kill-tier reasons are emitted in canonical order.

evidence.quote: - `mode_reasons` MUST include **all** active reasons from the **computed TradingMode tier** for that tick.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a Kill-tier multi-predicate AT that asserts full kill-reason completeness and canonical ordering.
